name: Microsoft Azure App Registration
description: Microsoft Azure App Registration is the Microsoft Entra ID configuration used to establish an application identity, tenant audience, redirect URIs, credentials and API permissions.
agentUseSummary: This identity setup is visible as a canonical Microsoft provider-family security preview. Relay will not collect tenant app secrets or expose generic Microsoft Graph access; Outlook, Teams, OneDrive and other actions remain in their typed canonical connectors.

capabilities.label: Use a tenant-managed application identity
capabilities.description: If customer-managed identity is approved, extend only the relevant canonical Microsoft connector with an exact tenant, audience, redirect, credential and least-privilege permission contract.

blocked.label: Create duplicate Microsoft provider state
blocked.description: An app-registration listing must not create a parallel token, tool or approval surface beside Relay's typed Microsoft product connectors.

blocked.label: Capture tenant application credentials
blocked.description: Relay will not ask a tenant user to paste a client secret, certificate private key or federated credential into this Marketplace alias.

blocked.label: Create or configure an Entra app registration
blocked.description: Tenant audience, owners, redirects, credentials, API permissions and property locks are identity-administration operations outside Relay agent actions.

blocked.label: Grant user or administrator consent
blocked.description: Delegated and application permissions have different data reach, and app-only permissions can access tenant data without a signed-in user; Relay will not grant them through an agent action.

blocked.label: Call arbitrary Microsoft Graph APIs
blocked.description: A generic Graph client would collapse unrelated resource permissions and bypass the typed bounds, approvals and audits of canonical providers.

approvalProfiles.label: Microsoft identity security review
approvalProfiles.description: This setup alias is not connectable. Tenant-managed credentials and permissions remain unavailable until a canonical connector has a workload-specific, least-privilege and revocable design.

runtimeSupport.description: This alias installs no OpenClaw tools; customer-managed identity must extend a canonical Microsoft provider pack.
This alias installs no Hermes tools; customer-managed identity must extend a canonical Microsoft provider pack.

providerSetup.blocker: Microsoft Entra app registrations can combine tenant audience, redirects, credentials and delegated or app-only permissions across unrelated APIs. Relay does not support customer-owned Entra credentials or generic Graph authority, and Microsoft warns misconfiguration can have organization-wide effects.
providerSetup.nextAction: Prefer Relay-owned identity on canonical Microsoft connectors. For an approved tenant-managed case, extend one connector with immutable tenant/client binding, exact redirects and permissions, delegated access where possible, workload identity federation or certificates instead of secrets, consent evidence, app-instance locks, ownership review, rotation and revocation.

evidence.supports: Microsoft documents tenant-specific app registration, supported account audiences, immutable home-tenant placement, application client IDs and administrator configuration.

Microsoft warns app-registration misconfiguration can have organization-wide effects and recommends least privilege, delegated access where possible, managed or federated identity, certificates over secrets, property locks and periodic review.
Microsoft distinguishes delegated permissions constrained by the signed-in user from administrator-consented application permissions that operate without a user and can reach tenant-wide data.
Microsoft documents certificates, federated identity credentials and client secrets for confidential clients and recommends certificates over secrets for production.
